name: Taha Mohammed
headline: Mechatronics engineer — robotics, control, embedded systems
availability: Open to remote and relocation · graduating 2027
shortBio: Final-year mechatronics engineer who builds machines end to end — the CAD, the board, the firmware, and the control loop that ties them together. I measure before I claim, and I document what broke.
longBio:
I'm a final-year mechatronics engineering student in Cairo, and I like the seam where disciplines meet: the point where a mechanism, a circuit and a control loop stop being three subjects and become one machine.

Most of what I know that matters didn't come from lectures. It came from a robotic arm that taught me why backlash is a budget line, a line-follower that taught me that data beats intuition every time you let it, and a farm gantry that is currently teaching me that "outdoor-adjacent" is a materials problem before it is a software one. Each project on this site records what was built, what broke, and what was measured — because that is the part I'd want to read in someone else's portfolio.

I'm graduating in 2027 and looking for a graduate role or internship in robotics, automation, or embedded systems — anywhere I'd ship hardware that has to work when nobody is watching it. Open to remote and to relocation.

Away from the bench I sketch mechanisms I have no budget to build, and I maintain the university robotics club's parts library, which future members will either thank me for or never notice. Both outcomes are fine.
